text:
Closest verified precedents cover parts of the proposal; no exact match established for a GRU hidden state plus gated recent-item embedding-pooling residual. [NARM (2017)](https://arxiv.org/html/1711.04725) combines the final GRU state with attention-pooled GRU states through concatenation, rather than a gated raw-embedding residual. Its Table 4 compares global-only, local-only and hybrid representations: DIGINETICA Recall@20 at dimension 100 is 61.88%, 61.71% and 62.58%, respectively. Crucially, local-only still uses recurrent states, so it does not establish that recent embedding pooling independently helps. [HGN (2019)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.09217) supplies related feature/instance gating of recent-item representations, but does not establish the proposed GRU-residual combination.

Shortcut concerns have empirical support. [Repetition and Exploration (2023)](https://staff.fnwi.uva.nl/m.derijke/wp-content/papercite-data/pdf/li-2023-repetition.pdf) finds repetition shortcuts and inherent repetitive bias, exacerbated by shared input/output embeddings; independent output embeddings alleviate it. This concerns repeat-item bias, not direct proof of last-item dependence. [Measuring Recency Bias (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) reports that excessive recency emphasis harms accuracy and that mitigation improves evaluated models. NARM’s attention examples also identify useful beginning/middle items, although visualizations alone cannot rule out shortcuts.

Recommended controls, rather than established findings: separately train GRU-only, pooling-only and combined ablations; compare last-item-only versus several-item pooling, exclude the last item from pooling, and shuffle earlier items while preserving the last. Match added parameters with a GRU-state MLP control. Compare fixed versus learned gates, normalized versus unnormalized residual branches, and near-closed versus neutral gate initialization; inspect gate saturation and branch norms. No verified controlled evidence located here establishes an optimal residual normalization or gate initialization. Keep every deployed category predictor a single jointly trained network.
